questInteractionRisk.failureTarget: Answer A: A child begs earnestly for one more chance.
questInteractionRisk.failureSummary: On each observed failure, a normal Playwright click reaches the visible/enabled/stable state for the same Quest answer, completes scroll-into-view, and then times out at 30000ms while performing the click action.
questInteractionRisk.sequenceIsolation: The target text is the known correct answer for vocab-transfer-plead. The QA case begins with exerciseWrongRetry, whose first two answer clicks intentionally choose a non-answer and whose third answer click chooses q.answer. Because the failure target is q.answer for the first current Quest, the evidence localizes the timeout to the assisted-correct click after the wrong/retry sequence rather than either intentional wrong click.

dailyPoolConfound.reason: src/gameModel.js dailyPool(date) seeds and shuffles the question bank with Math.floor(date / 86400000). The prior passing persistence run occurred before the 2026-09-23T00:00:00Z UTC day boundary, while all failing attempts occurred after it, so the prior PASS versus current FAIL comparison changes both motion commit and deterministic daily Quest content.

questInteractionRisk.motionAssessment: Treat the repeated timeout as a real final-QA interaction blocker, but do not make a speculative Workstream 11 runtime change yet. The latest Workstream 11 diff clears stale sbMotionCorrect/sbMotionStaticCue classes on non-correct feedback; on this first-question sequence there is no earlier correct state, so those removals are expected to be no-ops before the failing assisted-correct click. The failure also crosses a deterministic UTC daily-pool rollover relative to the older passing run. Current evidence therefore reproduces the blocker but does not isolate a motion/accessibility cause.

Workstream 11 should change motion only if that evidence isolates a motion/accessibility mutation or event-handler cause.
